selection_note: Only ONE candidate in the pool was both clean (zero unmapped) AND genuinely non-duplicate: Country Captain. Of the six 'clean' candidates the sourcer flagged as zero-unmapped, two are HARD catalog duplicates already live (Mississippi Pot Roast, Loco Moco), two are near-duplicates of live ground-beef dishes (Stroganoff, Beef and Broccoli), and the fifth (Marry Me Chicken) is a near-duplicate of the live creamy-sun-dried-tomato chicken cluster. Per this run's explicit 'ship two nobody can call duplicates over defending a borderline' directive, the #2 slot went to the strongest genuinely-distinct candidate (Chicken Florentine) even though it costs one new commodity (white wine), rather than shipping the zero-flag-but-callable-as-dupe Marry Me Chicken. No good cross-protein pair existed (the only non-chicken survivor, Pork Lo Mein, is flagged, weakest, and a 3rd-protein copy of an existing dish), so two chicken picks with maximal cuisine/flavor separation is the correct pairing.

selected.name: Country Captain Chicken
selected.why: Distinct cuisine the catalog lacks, curry-braise over rice, all commodities on hand.
selected.selector_note: Per-serving protein NOT published. Thighs plus bacon make 25g+ near-certain but unverified.
selected.dedup_verdict: SELECT. Genuinely distinct: no catalog neighbor. Nearest by ingredients are Chicken Kabsa and Chicken Maqluba (Middle-Eastern rice-cooked-in dishes, different plates) and the many catalog curries (Madras, Tikka Masala, Trinidadian, etc., all different profiles). Country Captain's curry-powder+garam braise with the raisin/almond/bell-pepper/bacon signature served OVER rice is its own dinner. Widens the American/Tex-Mex-skewed catalog the most (no Anglo-Indian entry exists). Clean (zero unmapped). Caveat carried: src_protein unpublished (thighs+bacon => 25g+ near-certain); 548 cal clears the 500 floor.

selected.name: Chicken Florentine
selected.why: Creamy spinach skillet; catalog has Turkey Florentine Rice Bake but no chicken skillet version. Strong macros.
selected.selector_note: FLAGGED: 3/4 cup dry white wine, omittable by swapping broth.
selected.dedup_verdict: SELECT. Least-duplicate of every remaining candidate. Its only namesake, Turkey Florentine Rice Bake, is a DIFFERENT protein (turkey) in a DIFFERENT format (rice-bake casserole vs a fresh skillet cutlet in cream sauce) — a genuinely different dinner by the judge-the-food rule. It carries NO sun-dried tomato, so unlike Marry Me it stays out of the live creamy-sun-dried-tomato chicken cluster (Tuscan Chicken Pasta / Italian Chicken Penne). Best macros of the flagged set (44g protein, 614 cal, no calorie caveat). Wins the #2 slot over the zero-flag Marry Me Chicken because this run weights 'nobody can call it a duplicate' above zero-flag when they conflict, and its single flag (white wine) is one clean new commodity (also omittable via broth).

rejected_dupes.name: Mississippi Pot Roast
rejected_dupes.reason: HARD catalog duplicate. Same dish, same protein, same name. The candidate's 'absent from catalog' claim is factually wrong: the digest already lists 'Mississippi Pot Roast Bowls' under beef. Not a distinct variation of anything - it IS the live recipe.

rejected_dupes.name: Loco Moco
rejected_dupes.dupe_of: Hawaiian Loco Moco Rice Bowls (live, beef)
rejected_dupes.reason: HARD catalog duplicate. Same dish (ground-beef patty + brown gravy + fried egg over rice), same protein, same cuisine. Already live as 'Hawaiian Loco Moco Rice Bowls' under beef.

rejected_dupes.name: Classic Beef Stroganoff
rejected_dupes.reason: Near-duplicate. Protein (beef), sauce family (sour-cream/mushroom stroganoff), starch (egg noodles), and method (skillet) all match the live ground-beef stroganoff - 4/4 on the dish axes, only ground vs sliced sirloin differs, which is not a distinct dinner. The catalog also already runs a whole-muscle stroganoff (Pork Tenderloin Stroganoff over Egg Noodles), so the 'whole-muscle is a new variation' argument is already spent. Callable as a dupe; benched per this run's bar.

rejected_dupes.name: Chinese Beef and Broccoli
rejected_dupes.dupe_of: Ground Beef and Broccoli Bowls (live, beef)
rejected_dupes.reason: Near-duplicate. Protein (beef), primary veg (broccoli), sauce family (soy/oyster Asian), and starch (rice bowl) all match the live 'Ground Beef and Broccoli Bowls'; only sliced flank vs ground differs. Same eaten plate. (Also adjacent to 'Cheesy Beef and Broccoli Rice Bowls', a different cheese-sauce build.) Callable as a dupe; benched per this run's bar.

borderline.name: Marry Me Chicken
near_dupe_of: Slow Cooker Tuscan Chicken Pasta (live, chicken)
Slow Cooker Italian Chicken Penne (live, chicken)
Marry Me Pork Chops over Pasta (live, pork - same sauce)
borderline.reason: Zero unmapped flags, but a near-duplicate of the live creamy-sun-dried-tomato-parmesan chicken pasta cluster. Protein (chicken), sauce/flavor (cream + parmesan + sun-dried tomato), and starch (short pasta) all match Tuscan Chicken Pasta and Italian Chicken Penne (3/4 - only slow-cooker-vs-skillet and coconut-milk-vs-heavy-cream differ), and the identical sauce ships on Marry Me Pork Chops. The plate is already on the menu three ways. Held out (not selected, not hard-killed): a skeptic can absolutely call it a duplicate, which fails this run's 'nobody can call it a dupe' bar, but the fresh-skillet execution is a fair argument for a distinct build, so the audit stage should adjudicate rather than have me silently drop it.

borderline.name: Chicken Fricassee
near_dupe_of: Slow Cooker Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Bowls (live, chicken)
borderline.reason: Near-duplicate of the live 'Slow Cooker Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Bowls' on the 3/4 test (chicken + creamy-mushroom sauce + rice/noodle starch; only skillet-vs-slow-cooker and cream/wine-vs-cream-cheese differ). Also the French-chicken lane is already well-populated (Coq au Vin, Chicken Provencal, Chicken Normandy, Slow Cooker French Onion Chicken), so it widens cuisine little. Plus a white-wine flag. Lost the #2 slot to Chicken Florentine, which is genuinely distinct AND has stronger macros.

borderline.name: Pork Lo Mein
near_dupe_of: Chicken Lo Mein Noodle Bowls (live, chicken)
borderline.reason: Same dish (lo mein - noodles in soy/oyster/sesame with veg) as two live entries, just a third protein. The catalog demonstrably runs multi-protein lo mein already, so a pork version is a defensible protein-variant rather than a hard dupe - but it is the pool's weakest candidate on the merits: flagged (water chestnuts unmapped, one new commodity), sourcer-called-weakest, and borderline published calories. Only non-chicken survivor, but too weak to be a 'good cross-protein pair', so it does not unseat two-chicken selection. Held for the audit stage.

shortfall_note: No numeric shortfall: 2 selected against a target of 2. Flagging for the orchestrator that the NON-DUPE pool was thin - only 1 of 9 candidates was clean-AND-distinct (Country Captain); the #2 pick required accepting one new commodity (white wine) to stay non-dupe. If a stricter zero-new-commodity constraint is required, the run is 1 short and more sourcing should run. Same-dish-different-protein twins noted for a cross-protein pass: Pork Lo Mein <-> Chicken/Turkey Lo Mein; Marry Me Chicken <-> Marry Me Pork Chops (same sauce).
